answer: Sybil resistance rests on a bonded stake each agent posts before its work counts. Collateral is sized to the value an identity can extract and slashed once a cluster proves to be one operator puppeteering many keys. A fake fleet must fund every seat up front, so cost scales linearly with identity count while payout stays capped per epoch and each extra puppet loses money. Honest agents reclaim their stake on exit; attackers watch theirs burn. Reputation builds like a slow ripple only real service makes, and no shortcut reaches the summit or the zenith without capital.
